The *Asaññakathā* (Kv 3.11) is a debate situated in the third vagga of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text discusses the nature of unconscious or non-percipient states (*asañña*), a subject connected in canonical tradition with the *Brahmajāla Sutta* (DN 1) of the Dīgha Nikāya, which SuttaCentral notes as referencing this topic [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation of the text [SuttaCentral]. The available secondary literature passages do not discuss this specific debate directly, instead addressing broader canonical occurrences of non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), meditative absorption, or homographic terms such as death-proximate (*āsanna*) karma.
